Step by step

  1. Someone asks

    Requests come in through one Deskline form, so IT stops getting them in direct messages, hallway chats and email.

  2. The app decides the approvers

    Everyday tools need the manager's yes. Apps holding finance, payroll or customer data also need the app owner.

  3. Access is granted with an end date

    Keyring grants the smallest role that fits the request, for 90 days by default.

  4. Everything is logged

    Who asked, why, who approved and when access was granted all land in one log your auditors can read.

  5. Nothing lingers

    Seven days before access ends, the owner is asked whether to renew. No answer means it expires.

When things don't go to plan

The exceptions are where manual processes break down. These are handled out of the box.

  • Manager is the requester

    approval goes to their own manager instead.

  • Request for an app Keyring doesn't manage

    it becomes a task for IT with the approvals already attached.

  • Employee changes team

    access granted for the old team is flagged for review.

  • Employee leaves

    every grant from this workflow is revoked the same day.
